findings.text: §35's leading candidate is "a launch from the queue that leaves the dispatch sidecar naming no run, so the delivery cannot be filed under a review run", yet the census it reports in the same paragraph counts 6 of 463 dispatched sidecars (7 with this review run) as unstored too, and one of those, `the-fleet-node-stays-in-service` composed `r-20261018T110703328217` launched `r-20261018T111535867952`, carries exactly the join's rewrite string "the queued review launched as run r-20261018T111535867952" and still has no record under `docs/state/reckon/reviews/plan/the-fleet-node-stays-in-service/` (5 sibling records from 2026-10-18 are present, so the absence is measured, not an unreadable store) — so a sidecar naming its launched run is not sufficient for the delivery to be filed, and "the sidecar names no run" is not the whole cause
